newsitem.title: CHINA: China to let non-financial entities issue bonds.
newsitem.headline: China to let non-financial entities issue bonds.

text.p: China will allow a group of non-financial entities to issue bonds overseas on an experimental basis, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday, quoting an official of the cabinet's State Planning Commission.

Those chosen should be in the country's pillar industries and have good records in debt repayment, profit earning and assets structure, said the official, who was not identified. They would be subject to regular examination.
He did not say when the firms would be chosen or if there would be a ceiling on the amount of bonds they could issue each year.
The new measure would cut the cost of raising funds abroad and help ease the demand for funds required by major national construction projects, the official said. He did not elaborate.

Currently the Ministry of Finance and a dozen qualified financial institutions are the only ones authorised to issue overseas debt notes. Funds raised overseas are then channelled into key construction projects and enterprises.
Between 1982 and April this year, China has issued a total of $18.7 billion worth of bonds overseas, Xinhua said.
